name: IL-08
label: Likely D

key_factors: D+5 district sits in a 2026 national environment favoring Democrats
Melissa Bean, who previously held this seat, has a large outside-spending edge (~$5.5M) against no Republican outside support
Prediction markets price Democrats at about 95%
Open seat with no public polling adds some uncertainty
model.rationale: The district's Democratic lean and a favorable national environment carry through even without Krishnamoorthi on the ballot; Bean's fundraising edge, heavy outside backing and Polymarket pricing near 95% keep Democrats firmly favored, with the absence of polling the main caveat.
model.watch: A late shift in the national environment toward Republicans, or a major GOP outside-spending push behind Davis, could tighten this open seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

Open seat: Raja Krishnamoorthi (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
IL-08 is an open suburban Chicago seat that has leaned Democratic by about five points. Raja Krishnamoorthi is leaving to run for Senate, and Democrats have turned to Melissa Bean, a former congresswoman who held this seat from 2005 to 2011. Republicans nominated Jennifer Davis, a first-time congressional candidate.

Bean has out-raised Davis and benefits from roughly $5.5 million in outside support, against essentially none for Davis. The national environment favors Democrats this cycle, and prediction markets price the seat at about 95 percent Democratic. No public general-election polls are available, so the forecast rests on district lean, candidate profiles and spending patterns. The open seat removes an incumbent's personal vote, but Democratic advantages in money, name recognition and environment keep this in Safe D territory, with only modest uncertainty.
